title: Buying A House
statementMd:
Zane the wizard had never loved anyone before, until he fell in love with a girl, whose name remains unknown to us.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d3d033c8aa4b077ead3b1a4d48bcd6a347e60710.png)

The girl lives in house $*m*$ of a village. There are $*n*$ houses in that village, lining in a straight line from left to right: house $1$, house $2$, ..., house $*n*$. The village is also well-structured: house $*i*$ and house $*i* + 1$ ($1 ≤ *i* < *n*$) are exactly $10$ meters away. In this village, some houses are occupied, and some are not. Indeed, unoccupied houses can be purchased.

You will be given $*n*$ integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ that denote the availability and the prices of the houses. If house $*i*$ is occupied, and therefore cannot be bought, then $*a*_{*i*}$ equals $0$. Otherwise, house $*i*$ can be bought, and $*a*_{*i*}$ represents the money required to buy it, in dollars.

As Zane has only $*k*$ dollars to spare, it becomes a challenge for him to choose the house to purchase, so that he could live as near as possible to his crush. Help Zane determine the minimum distance from his crush's house to some house he can afford, to help him succeed in his love.

## Input

The first line contains three integers $*n*$, $*m*$, and $*k*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$, $1 ≤ *m* ≤ *n*$, $1 ≤ *k* ≤ 100$) — the number of houses in the village, the house where the girl lives, and the amount of money Zane has (in dollars), respectively.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($0 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 100$) — denoting the availability and the prices of the houses.

It is guaranteed that $*a*_{*m*} = 0$ and that it is possible to purchase some house with no more than $*k*$ dollars.

## Output

Print one integer — the minimum distance, in meters, from the house where the girl Zane likes lives to the house Zane can buy.

## Note

In the first sample, with $*k* = 20$ dollars, Zane can buy only house $5$. The distance from house $*m* = 1$ to house $5$ is $10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 40$ meters.

In the second sample, Zane can buy houses $6$ and $7$. It is better to buy house $6$ than house $7$, since house $*m* = 3$ and house $6$ are only $30$ meters away, while house $*m* = 3$ and house $7$ are $40$ meters away.
statementZhMd:
Zane 这位巫师此前从未爱过任何人，直到他爱上了一个女孩，而我们还不知道她的名字。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d3d033c8aa4b077ead3b1a4d48bcd6a347e60710.png)

这个女孩住在村庄的房子 $*m*$ 中。这个村庄共有 $*n*$ 所房子，从左到右排成一条直线：房子 $1$、房子 $2$、……、房子 $*n*$。这个村庄的规划也很整齐：房子 $*i*$ 和房子 $*i* + 1$（$1 ≤ *i* < *n*$）之间恰好相距 $10$ 米。村庄中有些房子已经有人居住，有些则没有。事实上，无人居住的房子可以买下。

现在给你 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$，它们表示各所房子的可购买状态和价格。如果房子 $*i*$ 已有人居住，因此无法购买，那么 $*a*_{*i*}$ 等于 $0$。否则，房子 $*i*$ 可以购买，$*a*_{*i*}$ 表示购买它所需的钱数，单位为美元。

由于 Zane 只有 $*k*$ 美元可以使用，他需要选择一所房子购买，以便尽可能靠近自己心仪的女孩。请帮助 Zane 确定：在他能够负担的房子中，距离女孩所住房子最近的距离是多少，从而助他赢得爱情。

## 输入格式

第一行包含三个整数 $*n*$、$*m*$ 和 $*k*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$，$1 ≤ *m* ≤ *n*$，$1 ≤ *k* ≤ 100$）——村庄中的房子数量、女孩所住的房子编号，以及 Zane 拥有的钱数（单位为美元）。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$0 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 100$）——表示各所房子的可购买状态和价格。

保证 $*a*_{*m*} = 0$，并且一定存在一所价格不超过 $*k*$ 美元的房子可以买下。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——女孩所住房子与 Zane 能够购买的房子之间的最小距离，单位为米。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，当 $*k* = 20$ 美元时，Zane 只能购买房子 $5$。房子 $*m* = 1$ 与房子 $5$ 之间的距离为 $10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 40$ 米。

在第二个样例中，Zane 可以购买房子 $6$ 和 $7$。购买房子 $6$ 更好，因为房子 $*m* = 3$ 与房子 $6$ 之间只有 $30$ 米，而房子 $*m* = 3$ 与房子 $7$ 之间有 $40$ 米。
